strengths: The paper is well-written and easy to follow
The benchmark proposed in the paper contains 35 datasets
The datasets and implementations are shared as open-source
I believe this is the first work that attempts to unify and benchmark GLAD and GLOD tasks, the findings could be broadly interesting to the graph data mining community
the authors conducted extensive experiments and open-sourced their code base (which I believe is easy to extend), making contributions to future research
A large amount of datasets are employed to establish the benchmark to fairly compare the mutiple GLAD and GLOD emthods under a unified experimental setting.
In addition to the performance, the paper also investigates more characteristics of methods including generalizability, robustness, and efficiency.
The comprehensive benchmark and the multiple observations are provided in the experimental analysis to inspire future work.
There is no clear distinction between the training set and test set in unsupervised GLAD. Leveraging unsupervised graph-level anomaly detection methods for OOD detection is a good point.

The paper makes an original contribution by unifying GLAD and GLOD into a single benchmark, UB-GOLD. This creative combination highlights the conceptual overlap between the two tasks, simplifying evaluation in both areas.

The paper's experiments evaluate 18 methods on 35 datasets. It offers a multi-dimensional analysis. The breadth of datasets used ensures reliable, real-world applicability, while the open-source codebase.

UB-GOLD offers insights into detecting near-OOD samples and noisy training data. These findings current limitations in existing methods. What's more, this work focus on generalizability, robustness, and efficiency ensures the benchmark’s practical relevance across different application domains, making it a useful resource in the field.
weaknesses: The main findings of the paper are mostly expected
It is not clear why the same methods should solve anomaly detection and out-of-distribution detection
Most of the datasets are from the same domain
It is unclear how much can be learned from these results.
The unification of the tasks needs a more clear formalization than definition 1.
From Table 1, only 8/35 datasets are not molecules. This can bias the findings towards methods that perform well on molecules, which is something not discussed in the paper.
How are the hyperparameters of the methods set without a validation set? I was not able to understand this from Appendix D.
The authors should dedicate more space and effort to the unification process, specifically providing formal definitions of GLAD and GLOD with math symbols.
The relationship between GLAD and GLOD needs deeper discussion, including whether OOD detection is a broader concept than anomaly detection.
Missing details on how anomalies or OOD samples are defined or generated in each dataset.
Results are only provided for a subset of methods in Figures 4, 5, and 6; full results should be included in the appendix.
Metrics are not specified in Figures 4 and 5; clarification and complete results for all metrics are needed.
Hyperparameter search uses test set performance, raising concerns about practical applicability and potential overfitting.
The term 'generalisability' is used ambiguously and should be clarified or replaced.
Clarification is needed on how in-distribution test samples are constructed, including selection criteria and proportions.
The paper needs to explicitly clarify whether any data leakage occurs between training and test sets in the unsupervised setting and discuss its potential impact.
A more detailed analysis of the overlap between OOD samples is needed, with specific examples and reasons for pronounced overlaps in particular datasets.
The paper could benefit from a more in-depth discussion of why certain methods fail in specific scenarios.
A more concise summary section highlighting the most important findings from the multi-dimensional analyses should be added.
The unexpected poor performance of SSL-D and GK-D methods on datasets like IC50-Size needs explanation.
